Executive Summary

  • Interest rates tighten: A net 43.8% of Slovak firms reported tighter bank loan interest rates, rising 38.3 pp from a net 5.5% and exceeding both the EA (net 40.0%) and Germany (net 42.5%).
  • Financing split widens: The credit line gap widened to +15.3pp as need outpaced flat availability, even as the bank loan gap eased to -6.0pp — cheaper loan access and costlier liquidity coexist.
  • Cost-margin squeeze: Labour costs rose for a net 78.81% of Slovak firms, 19.85 pp above the EA, while turnover still fell for a net 12.83% despite improving 13.39 pp.
  • Turnover outlook lags: A net 6.75% of Slovak firms expected turnover to increase, down 14.15 pp from two waves earlier, against the EA's net 25.88% — a 19.1 pp gap.

Financing Conditions

Slovak interest rate tightening rose 38 pp, exceeding EA and DE

Changes in Terms and Conditions of Bank Financing (Q10)

  • A net 43.8% of Slovak firms (n=76) reported tighter interest rates, rising 38.3 pp from a net 5.5% in the previous wave — placing Slovakia above the EA (net 40.0%) and Germany (net 42.5%), heightening financing costs for borrowers.
  • A net 12.4% of Slovak firms (n=74) reported a reduction in available loan or credit line size, up 6.3 pp from the previous wave and above both the EA (net 9.1%) and DE (net 7.9%), constraining liquidity options.
  • Across the euro area (n=1,906), interest rate tightening also intensified, rising 12.7 pp to a net 40.0% of firms reporting higher rates, compared with a net 27.3% in the previous wave — signalling broader tightening pressures.

* Only firms that have used or applied for this type of financing in the past are asked this question. A lower n relative to the total sample is by design and does not indicate a data quality issue — see ECB SAFE methodology for details.

ⓘ SQL — bank_loan_terms.sql (cited column: net_balance_wtd)
-- Chart 1: Changes in terms and conditions of bank financing (Q10)
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Austria (AT), Germany (DE)
-- All firm sizes combined (firm_size = 'all'), last 4 waves
--
-- net_balance_wtd: positive = net tightening (adverse for firms)
--                 negative = net easing (favourable for firms)
-- Sub-items:
--   a = Level of interest rates
--   b = Non-interest financing costs (charges, fees, commissions)
--   c = Available size of loan or credit line
--   d = Available maturity of the loan
--   e = Collateral requirements
--   f = Other terms (guarantees, covenants, procedures)

WITH latest_waves AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT wave_number
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__financing_conditions
    WHERE question_id = 'q10'
    ORDER BY wave_number DESC
    LIMIT 4
)

SELECT
    f.wave_number,
    f.survey_period_label,
    f.country_code,
    f.sub_item,
    f.sub_item_label,
    f.net_balance_wtd,
    f.pct_improved_wtd,
    f.pct_deteriorated_wtd,
    f.pct_unchanged_wtd,
    f.n_respondents
FROM main_safe.mart_safe__financing_conditions f
WHERE f.question_id = 'q10'
  AND f.country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
  AND f.firm_size = 'all'
  AND f.wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
ORDER BY f.sub_item, f.country_code, f.wave_number

Credit line stress diverges sharply from easing bank loan conditions in Slovakia

Financing Need vs Availability Gap (Q5/Q9)

  • The Slovak credit line gap widened to +15.3pp (n=270), exceeding the EA's +14.0pp, as need rose to +15.2pp against near-flat availability (-0.1pp) — worsening access for firms.
  • Slovak trade credit stress reversed from +6.3pp to -1.7pp (n=180), as need fell from +7.1pp to -3.4pp, leaving Slovakia 12.7pp less stressed than the EA's +11.0pp gap.
  • The Slovak bank loan gap eased to -6.0pp (n=214) from -4.0pp in the previous wave, with availability rising from +1.4pp to +5.6pp, well below the EA's +2.8pp gap — signalling improving conditions.

* Only firms that have used or applied for this type of financing in the past are asked this question. A lower n relative to the total sample is by design and does not indicate a data quality issue — see ECB SAFE methodology for details.

ⓘ SQL — financing_gap.sql (cited column: financing_gap_wtd)
-- Financing need vs availability gap (Q5/Q9) from mart_safe__financing_conditions
-- financing_gap_wtd = Q5 net balance (need) minus Q9 net balance (availability)
-- Positive gap = need exceeds availability (adverse for firms)
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Germany (DE)
-- All firms (firm_size = 'all'), last 4 waves (dynamic)
--
-- Returns two result sets unioned:
--   type='main'  — bank loans (sub_item='a') for SK/EA/DE — used for the main grouped-bar chart
--   type='sk_all' — all major instruments for SK only — used for the SK instrument breakdown chart

WITH latest_waves AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT wave_number
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__financing_conditions
    WHERE question_id = 'q9'
    ORDER BY wave_number DESC
    LIMIT 4
),

q5 AS (
    SELECT wave_number, survey_period_label, country_code, sub_item, sub_item_label,
           net_balance_wtd AS need_nb, n_respondents AS n_respondents_need
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__financing_conditions
    WHERE question_id = 'q5'
      AND country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
      AND firm_size = 'all'
      AND wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
),

q9 AS (
    SELECT wave_number, country_code, sub_item,
           net_balance_wtd        AS availability_nb,
           financing_gap_wtd,
           n_respondents          AS n_respondents_avail
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__financing_conditions
    WHERE question_id = 'q9'
      AND country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
      AND firm_size = 'all'
      AND wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
),

joined AS (
    SELECT
        q5.wave_number,
        q5.survey_period_label,
        q5.country_code,
        q5.sub_item,
        q5.sub_item_label,
        q5.need_nb,
        q9.availability_nb,
        q9.financing_gap_wtd,
        q5.n_respondents_need,
        q9.n_respondents_avail
    FROM q5
    JOIN q9 USING (wave_number, country_code, sub_item)
)

-- Main chart: bank loans (a), credit lines (f), trade credit (b) for SK/EA/DE
SELECT *, 'main' AS chart_type
FROM joined
WHERE sub_item IN ('a', 'f', 'b')

UNION ALL

-- SK instrument breakdown: all instruments for Slovakia only
SELECT *, 'sk_all' AS chart_type
FROM joined
WHERE country_code = 'SK'
  AND sub_item IN ('a', 'b', 'f', 'g', 'h')

ORDER BY chart_type, sub_item, country_code, wave_number

Slovak bank loan availability expectations diverged from EA trend in wave 39

Expected Availability of External Financing (Q23)

  • A net 6.5% of Slovak firms (n=104) expected bank loan availability to deteriorate, worsening 1.3 pp from wave 38, while EA expectations improved 1.5 pp to a net 2.4% expecting deterioration — suggesting tighter domestic credit conditions ahead.
  • Slovak firms' trade credit availability expectations improved, with the net share expecting deterioration falling from 10.2% to 6.2% (n=90), compared with the EA's net 1.9% — easing pressure on liquidity chains.
  • Credit line availability expectations for Slovak firms (n=136) eased 3.2 pp to a net 3.9% expecting deterioration, approaching the EA's net 2.3% — reducing near-term financing risks.

* Only firms that have used or applied for this type of financing in the past are asked this question. A lower n relative to the total sample is by design and does not indicate a data quality issue — see ECB SAFE methodology for details.

† Observations with fewer than 10 valid responses in a given wave × country × sub-item cell are excluded from the chart; gaps in series indicate insufficient data for that period.

ⓘ SQL — availability_expectations.sql (cited column: net_balance_wtd)
-- Q23: Expected availability of external financing over the next quarter
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Germany (DE)
-- All firms (firm_size = 'all'), last 4 waves (dynamic)
--
-- net_balance_wtd: % expecting improvement minus % expecting deterioration
-- Positive = more firms expect availability to IMPROVE (FAVOURABLE)
-- Negative = more firms expect availability to DETERIORATE (ADVERSE)
--
-- Sub-items (matching Q5/Q9 instruments):
--   b = Bank loans
--   d = Trade credit
--   g = Credit lines and bank overdraft

WITH latest_waves AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT wave_number
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__availability_expectations
    ORDER BY wave_number DESC
    LIMIT 4
)

SELECT
    f.wave_number,
    f.survey_period_label,
    f.country_code,
    f.sub_item,
    f.sub_item_label,
    f.net_balance_wtd,
    f.pct_improve_wtd,
    f.pct_deteriorate_wtd,
    f.n_respondents
FROM main_safe.mart_safe__availability_expectations f
WHERE f.country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
  AND f.firm_size = 'all'
  AND f.n_respondents >= 10
  AND f.wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
ORDER BY f.sub_item, f.country_code, f.wave_number

Slovak fixed investment financing rose, closing gap with euro area

Purpose of Financing (Q6A)

  • Fixed investment financing rose from 34.2% to 40.7% among Slovak firms (n=242), a 6.5 pp increase that brought Slovakia above the EA's 38.4% — suggesting stronger capital expenditure plans.
  • Inventory and working capital remained the top financing purpose for Slovak firms at 57.0% (n=242), 16.2 pp above the EA's 40.8% — indicating persistent liquidity needs.
  • Refinancing or paying off obligations fell from 21.5% to 17.0% among Slovak firms (n=241), narrowing the gap with the EA's 15.8%.
ⓘ SQL — financing_purpose.sql (cited column: pct_cited_wtd)
-- Q6A: Purpose of financing (multi-select)
-- pct_cited_wtd = % of firms citing each purpose (can sum > 100% as multi-select)
-- purposes: 1=Fixed investment, 2=Inventory/working capital, 3=Hiring/training,
--           4=New products/services, 5=Refinancing, 6=Other
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Germany (DE)
-- All firms (firm_size = 'all'), last 4 waves (dynamic)

WITH latest_waves AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT wave_number
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__financing_purpose
    ORDER BY wave_number DESC
    LIMIT 4
)

SELECT
    f.wave_number,
    f.survey_period_label,
    f.country_code,
    f.purpose_id,
    f.purpose_label,
    f.pct_cited_wtd,
    f.n_respondents
FROM main_safe.mart_safe__financing_purpose f
WHERE f.country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
  AND f.firm_size = 'all'
  AND f.wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
ORDER BY f.purpose_id, f.country_code, f.wave_number

Bank willingness to lend holds steady in Slovakia above EA

Factors Affecting Access to External Financing (Q11)

  • A net 7.8% of Slovak firms (n=310) reported improved bank willingness to provide credit, unchanged from the previous wave and above the EA's net 5.6% (n=6,350) — suggesting stable credit supply conditions.
  • Access to public financial support improved notably in Slovakia, with the net balance rising from -33.8% to -21.2% (n=310), compared with a marginal easing from -15.5% to -13.6% in the EA — easing pressure on firms reliant on guarantees.
  • The general economic outlook deteriorated further for a net 51.6% of Slovak firms (n=472), worsening by 7.2 pp from the previous wave and running 22.2 pp below the EA's net 29.4%.
ⓘ SQL — financing_factors.sql (cited column: net_balance_wtd)
-- Q11: Self-assessed factors affecting availability of external financing
-- Net balance = % reporting improvement minus % reporting deterioration
-- Positive = factor improving (favourable for financing access)
-- Negative = factor deteriorating (adverse / potential credit supply constraint)
--
-- Key sub-items for credit supply analysis:
--   f = Willingness of banks to provide credit  (direct bank supply signal)
--   a = General economic outlook                (macro drag on supply)
--   b = Access to public financial support      (policy/guarantee channel)
--
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Germany (DE)
-- All firms (firm_size = 'all'), last 4 waves (dynamic)

WITH latest_waves AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT wave_number
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__financing_factors
    ORDER BY wave_number DESC
    LIMIT 4
)

SELECT
    f.wave_number,
    f.survey_period_label,
    f.country_code,
    f.sub_item,
    f.sub_item_label,
    f.net_balance_wtd,
    f.pct_improved_wtd,
    f.pct_deteriorated_wtd,
    f.n_respondents
FROM main_safe.mart_safe__financing_factors f
WHERE f.country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
  AND f.firm_size = 'all'
  AND f.sub_item IN ('f', 'a', 'b')
  AND f.wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
ORDER BY f.sub_item, f.country_code, f.wave_number

Economic Situation of Firms

Slovak turnover improved but remained negative as EA expanded

Business Situation Indicators (Q2)

  • A net 12.83% of Slovak firms (n=242) reported falling turnover, improving by 13.39 pp from the prior wave's net 26.22%, while the EA posted a net 8.11% increase — suggesting tentative recovery signs.
  • A net 34.38% of Slovak firms (n=242) reported falling profits, improving by 5.42 pp from the prior wave but remaining 19 pp more negative than the EA's net 15.39% decline.
  • Labour costs rose for a net 78.81% of Slovak firms (n=242), easing 4.81 pp from the prior wave but still 19.85 pp above the EA's net 58.96% — squeezing margins further.
ⓘ SQL — business_situation.sql (cited column: net_balance_wtd)
-- Q2: Business situation indicators (turnover, labour costs, profit, investment, employees)
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Germany (DE)
-- All firms (firm_size = 'all'), last 4 waves (dynamic)
--
-- sub_items: a=Turnover, b=Labour costs, e=Profit, g=Investment, i=Employees
-- Sign: positive = indicator rising; labour costs positive = costs rising (adverse)

WITH latest_waves AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT wave_number
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__business_situation
    ORDER BY wave_number DESC
    LIMIT 4
)

SELECT
    f.wave_number,
    f.survey_period_label,
    f.country_code,
    f.sub_item,
    f.sub_item_label,
    f.net_balance_wtd,
    f.pct_increased_wtd,
    f.pct_decreased_wtd,
    f.n_respondents
FROM main_safe.mart_safe__business_situation f
WHERE f.country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
  AND f.firm_size = 'all'
  AND f.wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
ORDER BY f.sub_item, f.country_code, f.wave_number

Slovak turnover outlook fell while euro area expectations rose

Expected Changes in Turnover and Investment (Q26)

  • A net 6.75% of Slovak firms (n=228) expected turnover to increase, down 14.15 pp from two waves earlier, while the euro area rose to a net 25.88% — widening the SK–EA gap to 19.1 pp, signalling weaker Slovak competitiveness.
  • Slovak fixed investment expectations rose to a net 14.67% (n=228), up 3.88 pp from two waves earlier, outpacing the euro area's net 9.45% and reversing the relative positions of the two regions — suggesting catch-up potential.
  • Euro area and German turnover outlooks both improved from two waves earlier, reaching net 25.88% and net 19.08% respectively, confirming Slovakia as the regional outlier on turnover pessimism — highlighting structural challenges.

‡ This question is not fielded every quarter — consecutive points on this chart may be more than one quarter apart. See point labels for the actual survey period.

ⓘ SQL — outlook.sql (cited column: net_balance_wtd)
-- Q26: Expected changes in turnover and investments over the next two quarters
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Germany (DE)
-- All firms (firm_size = 'all'), last 4 waves (dynamic)
--
-- net_balance_wtd: positive = more firms expect increase (FAVOURABLE)
--                 negative = more firms expect decrease (ADVERSE)
-- Sub-items:
--   a = Company's turnover
--   b = Investments in property, plant or equipment

WITH latest_waves AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT wave_number
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__outlook
    ORDER BY wave_number DESC
    LIMIT 4
)

SELECT
    f.wave_number,
    f.survey_period_label,
    f.country_code,
    f.sub_item,

WHERE f.country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
  AND f.firm_size = 'all'

Slovak firms face margin compression as input costs far outpace selling prices

Price, Wage and Employment Expectations (Q31/Q34)

  • Slovak firms (n=224) expected production input prices to rise 7.33% over the next 12 months, 3.58 pp above their 3.75% selling price expectation (n=222), pointing to ongoing margin compression.
  • Slovak firms anticipated average wage growth of 4.12% (n=233), 1.52 pp above the euro area's 2.60% (n=4,941), with both input price and wage expectations exceeding selling price expectations — signalling higher cost pressures.
  • Slovak firms' 12-month inflation expectations eased to 4.68% (n=193), down 0.29 pp from wave 38's 4.97%, remaining 0.80 pp above the euro area's 3.88% mean.

† Observations with fewer than 10 valid responses in a given wave × country × sub-item cell are excluded from the chart; gaps in series indicate insufficient data for that period.

ⓘ SQL — expectations_quantitative.sql (cited column: mean_wtd)
-- Q31/Q34: Quantitative expectations — inflation rate (Q31) and expected % changes
-- in selling prices, input costs, wages, employment (Q34).
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Germany (DE)
-- All firms (firm_size = 'all'), last 4 waves (dynamic)
--
-- mean_wtd: weighted mean expected % change (NOT a net balance)
-- Positive = firms expect an increase; negative = firms expect a decrease.
--
-- Sub-items:
--   Q31_a = Expected inflation rate in 12 months
--   Q34_a = Average selling price of products/services
--   Q34_b = Average prices of production inputs (non-labour)
--   Q34_c = Average wage of employees
--   Q34_d = Number of employees
--
-- panel_id = question_id || '_' || sub_item to disambiguate Q31/Q34 sub_item 'a'

WITH latest_waves AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT wave_number
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__expectations
    WHERE question_id = 'q34'
    ORDER BY wave_number DESC
    LIMIT 4
)

SELECT
    f.wave_number,
    f.survey_period_label,
    f.country_code,
    f.question_id,
    f.sub_item,
    f.question_id || '_' || f.sub_item                          AS panel_id,
    f.sub_item_label,
    f.mean_wtd,
    f.p25_unwtd,
    f.median_unwtd,
    f.p75_unwtd,
    f.n_respondents
FROM main_safe.mart_safe__expectations f
WHERE f.country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
  AND f.firm_size = 'all'
  AND f.question_id IN ('q31', 'q34')
  AND f.sub_item IN ('a', 'b', 'c', 'd')
  AND f.mean_wtd IS NOT NULL
  AND f.n_respondents >= 10
  AND f.wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
ORDER BY f.question_id, f.sub_item, f.country_code, f.wave_number

Slovak firms see upside inflation risk above the euro area average

Inflation Risk Outlook (Q33)

  • A net 61.2% of Slovak firms (n=242) saw upside risks to five-year inflation expectations, 7.2 pp above the euro area's net 54.0% (n=5,087) in wave 39 — implying tighter cost pressures for Slovak firms than peers.
  • The SK–EA divergence widened as Slovak firms' net balance rose mildly by 2.3 pp from wave 38, while the euro area's net balance eased by 1.3 pp over the same period — suggesting growing divergence in inflation expectations.
  • German firms reported a net 51.3% upside inflation risk, remaining below both Slovakia and the euro area aggregate in wave 39.

† Observations with fewer than 10 valid responses in a given wave × country × sub-item cell are excluded from the chart; gaps in series indicate insufficient data for that period.

ⓘ SQL — expectations_risk.sql (cited column: net_balance_wtd)
-- Q33: Main risk to 5-year inflation outlook (ordinal net balance)
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Germany (DE)
-- All firms (firm_size = 'all'), last 4 waves (dynamic)
--
-- net_balance_wtd: % seeing upside inflation risk minus % seeing downside risk
-- Positive = more firms see inflation as a risk to the upside
-- Negative = more firms see inflation risk to the downside

WITH latest_waves AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT wave_number
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__expectations
    WHERE question_id = 'q33'
    ORDER BY wave_number DESC
    LIMIT 4
)

SELECT
    f.wave_number,
    f.survey_period_label,
    f.country_code,
    f.pct_downside_wtd,
    f.pct_balanced_wtd,
    f.pct_upside_wtd,
    f.net_balance_wtd,
    f.n_respondents
FROM main_safe.mart_safe__expectations f
WHERE f.country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
  AND f.firm_size = 'all'
  AND f.question_id = 'q33'
  AND f.n_respondents >= 10
  AND f.wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
ORDER BY f.country_code, f.wave_number

Skilled staff shortage overtakes costs as Slovak firms' top concern

Most Pressing Business Problems (Q0B)

  • Slovak firms (n=239) rated skilled staff availability as the most pressing of the seven tested problems, scoring 6.64/10 — up 0.57 from 6.07 in the previous wave, now above the EA's 6.57, underscoring a growing operational bottleneck.
  • Costs of production or labour scored 6.62/10 (n=240), rising 0.43 from 6.19 in the previous wave, ranking second among the seven tested problems for Slovak firms — highlighting persistent inflationary pressures.
  • Regulation scored 6.10/10 (n=236), easing marginally by 0.08 from the previous wave, yet remaining above the EA average of 5.87 — suggesting lingering compliance burdens for firms.
ⓘ SQL — business_problems.sql (cited column: avg_pressingness_wtd)
-- Q0B: Most pressing business problems
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Germany (DE)
-- All firms (firm_size = 'all'), last 4 waves (dynamic)

WITH latest_waves AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT wave_number
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__business_problems
    ORDER BY wave_number DESC
    LIMIT 4
)

SELECT
    f.wave_number,
    f.survey_period_label,
    f.country_code,
    f.problem_id,
    f.problem_label,
    f.avg_pressingness_wtd,
    f.n_respondents
FROM main_safe.mart_safe__business_problems f
WHERE f.country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
  AND f.firm_size = 'all'
  AND f.wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
ORDER BY f.problem_id, f.country_code, f.wave_number

Source: ECB SAFE microdata. Net balance = % reporting increase minus % reporting decrease. Positive = tightening/rising (adverse for firms unless noted). Negative = easing/falling.
